review_notes:
I read the whole file and checked its non-theorem definitions against Mathlib. These were `unitF`, `archIdele` and `ofRealAt`. I also looked for existing Mathlib counterparts of the places where the file uses `InfinitePlace.Completion`.

- `unitF` is `Units.map (algebraMap (𝓞 F) F)`. This is a thin named specialisation of an existing operation. Mathlib has no named equivalent for the number-field units map. The only `Units.map (algebraMap …)` uses I found are in `CMField.lean`, and they are inline. I treated `unitF` as a legitimate named helper.
- `ofRealAt` embeds ℝ into `w.Completion`. It is built from Mathlib's `ringEquivRealOfIsReal` and `ringEquivComplexOfIsComplex`. I found no Mathlib `ℝ →+* w.Completion` map or `Algebra ℝ w.Completion` instance. Mathlib's `Algebra R v.Completion` instance is for an `R` that is already an algebra over `K`, which ℝ is not.
- `archIdele` and `ofRealAt` are also redefined in other project files, for example `S_AutomorphicForm_exists_forall_mem_centreCutSiegelSet_globalPoints_mul_mem_centreCutSiegelSetAmple.lean` and `S_AutomorphicForm_WindowedSiegel_exists_isCompact_cover_of_archHeight_le.lean`. Those are project-internal copies, not Mathlib duplicates. The only Mathlib-adjacent `archIdele` I found takes a real number `t`, so it is a different concept. I did not report these.
- The helper theorems in the file are standalone lemmas, which the rubric excludes: `norm_ringEquivRealOfIsReal'`, `norm_ringEquivComplexOfIsComplex'`, `exists_unit_log_balance`, `exists_int_translate_le`, `im_xCoord_eq_zero` and similar.

The one uncertainty is that I did not compare `archIdele` against every project definition of the same name. Even if I had, those would not count as Mathlib competitors under this rubric.
